Attempt-1's CLI entry-point guard bug is genuinely FIXED and independently re-verified in this review (not just trusted from the implementer's report): a standalone script run via node on this repo's own win32 machine confirms `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` evaluates true (both sides normalize to file:///C:/...), while the OLD naive `file://${process.argv[1]}` template literal evaluates false (produces file://C:\... with backslashes, no third slash) -- reproducing exactly the attempt-1 bug and confirming the fix resolves it identically across all three files (provision.mjs, capture.mjs, compare.mjs share the identical guard). Independently re-running `node plugins/relay/scripts/visual/provision.mjs` directly now measurably enters the guarded block (259ms, real named exit code 3) instead of attempt-1's bogus instant exit-0 (~0.13s) -- proving the guard now correctly dispatches into provision(). However, tracing why it returned PROVISION_FAILED_OTHER surfaced a SECOND, previously-hidden HIGH-severity Windows bug in the same file, masked until now by the first bug (attempt-1's broken guard meant provision() never actually ran, so this defect never had a chance to surface): isChromiumInstalled() (lines 46-50) and provision()'s real install attempt (lines 73-77) both call execFileAsync('npx', [...]) without { shell: true }. On Windows, npx resolves to npx.cmd, and Node's execFile/execFileAsync cannot invoke .cmd/.bat shims without shell:true -- independently reproduced in this review: execFileAsync('npx', ['--version'], {timeout:10000}) throws 'spawn npx ENOENT' on this machine even though `npx --version` succeeds fine interactively (v11.13.0), and adding { shell: true } to the identical call resolves it cleanly. Consequently BOTH execFileAsync calls always throw ENOENT on Windows; isChromiumInstalled() always returns false via its catch-swallow; the real install attempt's catch matches the ENOENT message against NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS (none match -- 'spawn npx ENOENT' contains none of ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET/ETIMEDOUT/EAI_AGAIN/getaddrinfo/network/403), falling through to PROVISION_FAILED_OTHER (code 3) regardless of whether Chromium is actually installed or the network is reachable -- exactly what this session's direct CLI run reproduced. This defeats the exit-code taxonomy's own documented purpose ('named exit codes distinguishing network-blocked vs. other failure', Task 2 ACTION spec + the PRD's Technical Risk mitigation) since the true root cause is neither a network failure nor a genuine 'other' provisioning failure -- it is a subprocess-invocation bug. Downstream, visual-verifier.md Step 1 branches ANY non-zero/unrecognized provision.mjs exit to DEGRADED_PROVISION_FAILED and permanently skips Step 2 (capture+compare), so on this repo's own win32 platform the FULL rung (real per-frame pixel diff scores) can never be reached regardless of true Chromium/network state -- AC-A3's success signal ('a real implementation attempt produces a fidelity-report.json with per-frame scores') can only ever be satisfied via the degraded-mode stub (diff_percent: null), never a genuine pixel diff, on Windows. Separately assessed per this round's explicit scope question: the missing plugins/relay/scripts/visual/node_modules (pngjs/pixelmatch/playwright not npm-installed) is judged a LEGITIMATE, non-blocking scope call, not a defect -- confirmed empirically absent via directory listing, but Task 1's package.json is deliberately self-contained/not-auto-installed by design (explicit ACTION text: 'a non-Figma project/clone of this repo never pays the Playwright/Chromium install cost'); none of the plan's Level 1/2/3 Validation Commands require the dependencies (all independently re-run in this review and confirmed PASS -- node --check is syntax-only, no module resolution needed); this repo's own plan Metadata confirms design_source/figma_track do not apply to this repo, so no real end-to-end invocation is expected here; installation is correctly deferred to a downstream Figma-track-enabled consumer project. Findings below are scoped to the newly-surfaced execFileAsync shell:true defect only -- the guard fix itself is confirmed correct and is not re-listed as a finding.

Attempt-2's sole HIGH-severity finding (execFileAsync('npx', [...]) throwing ENOENT on Windows in provision.mjs, defeating the exit-code taxonomy) is independently re-verified FIXED in this review, not just trusted from the implementer's report. Confirmed via direct diff of attempt-2 vs attempt-3 patches that attempt 3 changes ONLY provision.mjs -- both execFileAsync call sites (isChromiumInstalled, and provision()'s real install attempt) switched from execFile('npx',[args],...) to exec('npx playwright install --dry-run chromium', ...) / exec('npx playwright install --with-deps chromium', ...); capture.mjs and compare.mjs are byte-identical to attempt 2 and (re-confirmed via grep) contain zero child_process usage, so they never shared the pattern. Empirically reproduced the baseline bug in this session: execFileAsync('npx',['--version']) still throws 'spawn npx ENOENT' on this machine, while the new exec('npx --version') succeeds (stdout '11.13.0'), confirming the mechanism of the fix. Ran node provision.mjs directly end-to-end via spawnSync: real exit code 0 in 9739ms -- decisively a genuine dispatch into provision()/isChromiumInstalled() (not attempt-1's bogus ~130ms no-op, nor an ENOENT throw), proving the fix resolves the reported defect on this repo's own win32 platform. Injection-safety re-checked per this round's explicit ask: both exec() command strings ('npx playwright install --dry-run chromium' and 'npx playwright install --with-deps chromium') are fixed literals with zero interpolated/user-controlled/template segments -- no argument, env value, or file-derived string is concatenated into either command -- so the switch from execFile+args-array to exec+string introduces no shell-injection surface. The DEP0190-avoidance rationale in the code comment is also accurate: exec() takes a single pre-formed string with no args array, so Node's args-concatenation-under-shell deprecation warning (which execFile+shell:true+array would trip) does not apply. Two pre-existing, unchanged-since-attempt-1, non-blocking low-severity observations noted for the record (not failing the rubric): (a) visual-verifier.md Step 2's prose branches capture.mjs's non-zero exit only on the explicit CAPTURE_FAILED_DEV_SERVER_TIMEOUT stderr signal, leaving a non-timeout per-frame capture failure's classification to the dispatched agent's own judgment rather than an explicit branch, mitigated by Hard Constraint 4's fail-toward-safer-degraded-rung bias; (b) compare.mjs's applyMasks loop has no bounds check against PNG width/height, so a mask region exceeding frame dimensions would silently truncate (Buffer index writes past length are silent no-ops in Node, not a crash) rather than error -- masks are Design-Spec-authored geometry, not attacker-controlled input, so this is a correctness edge case, not a security concern.
